## Why (agent-DX defect class, 2026-07-11 maintainer DX directive)
Every entry in the maintainer-agent gotchas ledger about output exists because commands negotiated their own contracts: `pm search` takes `--format json|toon` only (`--format table` errors and looks like zero hits), `pm validate`/`pm notes` take `--json` only (wrong flag looks like zero notes), `pm list --json` projects, `pm get --json` wraps under `.item`, comments/notes bodies live at `.text`, `pm activity` ships an always-empty `.activity` decoy next to `.compact_activity` (pm-p3x4). Agents pay for this in retries and silent-empty misreads — the traps ARE the DX problem, per-command memorization is the tax.

## What
One flag grammar (same spelling, same accepted values, same default) and one envelope specification (documented shapes for list/get/mutation/diagnostic/annotation results) applied across every command. TOON and JSON stay; projections stay; nothing is removed — existing spellings become aliases tracked by the alias shim (pm-0z7n) with deprecation counters (pm-0mox).

## Sequencing
Land AFTER ADR pm-pbyu acceptance and on top of the pm-0z7n shim (flags are spellings too); coordinate with pm-cfed (lean JSON redesign — one envelope spec should serve both) and pm-gdi7 (unknown-option suggestions). Walk the full wiring checklist per surface change; token before/after via pm-a22j baseline.
Uniform output contract: one format-flag grammar + one envelope spec across every command (JSON/TOON), old spellings alias-preserved

Every command accepts one identical output-format flag contract; a single written envelope spec covers all read/mutation/diagnostic shapes; the per-command trap class is gone (search --format-only vs notes/validate --json-only vs activity .activity decoy); zero feature loss: all current spellings kept as deprecation-tracked aliases; contract tests assert flag+envelope parity across the full surface

One spec covers both the envelope shape and the exit-code semantics; the pm-0z7n alias deprecation fields (ledger lever b) also land in this spec.

Input-side MCP shape parity (pm_copy flat camelCase) also landed via pm-hno5 using the derive-from-flag-contracts pattern — that pattern (schemas generated from *_FLAG_CONTRACTS, never hand-declared) is the recommended mechanism for srns's envelope convergence too.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Token-efficiency doctrine, drafted 2026-07-25 to give the individual output items one ordered account of where agent tokens actually go and which lever addresses each. Measured baseline for orientation: the MCP tool surface alone costs roughly 8.2k tokens cold (28 tools, 32,979 bytes), and JSON costs 48-53 percent more than TOON for the same payload.

The levers, ordered by measured or expected saving per unit of implementation cost:

1. Do not send what the caller already has. The largest remaining waste is repeat orientation: an agent re-reads a workspace that has not changed. Owned by the delta read projection filed as pm-tuadp2; an unchanged workspace should cost a header and a count, not a projection.
2. Do not send what the caller did not ask for. Lean output shipped (null/empty omission, lean mutation echo, tag folding, counts-only validate, omitted-note counts). The remaining gap is that omission is per-command rather than contract-declared, which is exactly what pm-srns's single envelope spec fixes.
3. Send a ceiling, not a hope. Contract-declared per-command budgets with a deterministic degradation ladder, owned by pm-5t33or. Unbounded output is the failure mode that turns one bad call into a lost context window.
4. Send structure once. TOON's header-once tabular form already does this for rows; the same principle is unexploited for nested facets, where each item repeats its facet keys. A facet-table projection is the natural extension and belongs to the same envelope spec.
5. Do not make the caller ask twice. Round trips cost more than payload: an envelope that omits a count forces a second call, a blocked summary without blocker ids forces a second call, an error without the valid domain forces a retry. Several tracked issues are instances of this one principle, and the envelope spec should state it as a rule: every response either answers the obvious follow-up or names the exact call that will.
6. Move stable context out of the tool channel entirely. MCP resources and prompts, filed as pm-yf07b7, let the host carry orientation without a model-initiated call and without growing the tool count that costs roughly 500 cold-start tokens per tool.
7. Charge the session, not the call. Per-call budgets misallocate across a session; catalog entry (27) on pm-4k6b proposes the allocation policy that makes early orientation expensive and repeat orientation nearly free.

Anti-lever, recorded so it is not proposed again: shortening field names to save bytes. The measured saving is small against TOON's header-once form, and it costs the scripting contract its stable machine-readable names, which pm-psy1 guarantees and which every jq pipeline in the ecosystem depends on. Compress structure and redundancy, never identifiers.

Measurement discipline: every lever above must be argued against pm-8pnj (tokens per completed task) rather than against payload bytes in isolation, because levers 5 and 7 trade payload for round trips and only the task-level number captures that correctly.
